fields.description: Each field's unit, type and, where a wrong guess is expensive, its sign convention -- once per response rather than on every field object. `var` is positive WEST, the opposite of the WMM convention.

Credit.description: One data source, credited as the nav log's footer credits it.

Arrival.description: The ETA column as figures, one per leg. The `eta` field is the cell's text; this is the arithmetic behind it.

RenderCheckpoint.description: One checkpoint on the timeline, with what its card shows.

dev.description: added to magnetic; compass heading = magnetic heading + deviation
dev.title: deviation

eta.description: the cell's own text: elapsed time written like an ete ("1h20") when no departure time is set, a clock time ("15:20Z") when one is. The figures behind it are `arrivals` in GET /plans/{id}/render
eta.title: arrival

ete.description: a duration as text: m:ss under an hour, held to ten seconds ("4:40"); HhMM from an hour ("1h20"). A colon is always minutes:seconds, and a bare number written to the API is minutes
ete.title: leg time

fuel_burn.description: gallons burned on this leg, not a rate
fuel_burn.title: fuel burn

var.description: positive is WEST; magnetic heading = true heading + variation. Note this is the opposite of the WMM/IGRF convention, which is positive east
var.title: variation

wca.description: positive turns right; true heading = true course + wca
wca.title: wind-correction angle

wind_dir.description: degrees TRUE, and the direction the wind blows FROM
wind_dir.title: wind direction

fields.description: Each field's unit, type and, where a wrong guess is expensive, its sign convention -- once per response rather than on every field object. `var` is positive WEST, the opposite of the WMM convention.

origin.description: The kept plan this one was loaded from, which saving the working sheet writes to. Null for a plan loaded from nothing. Read-only.

passed_steps.description: Guide steps the pilot has looked at and moved past. A plain array, not a field object: nothing suggests a pass and nothing can disagree with one. Read-only.

working_sheet.description: True for the plan this account is in the middle of but has not kept.

RenderTerrain.description: The terrain profile as an SVG view box. Point lists are SVG `points` strings in view-box units; layers paint back to front: night, airspace, terrain, sea level, clouds, the red minimum-safe floor, the flight line.

sea_level.description: `{y}`, the sea-level line, when the route runs below it; else null.

fields.description: Each field's unit, type and, where a wrong guess is expensive, its sign convention -- once per response rather than on every field object. `var` is positive WEST, the opposite of the WMM convention.

WriteOutcome.description: What became of one write. Read `state`, not `value`: a value renders straight off the sheet whether the write landed or a suggester overtook it.

fields.description: Each field's unit, type and, where a wrong guess is expensive, its sign convention -- once per response rather than on every field object. `var` is positive WEST, the opposite of the WMM convention.

WriteBody.description: An object of sections, each an object of fields. Every field present is a write -- there is no `_target` to send. A bare scalar means `{"value": …}`; null or "" clears. One bad path refuses the whole body.

legs.description: Keyed by row index, as a string: "0" is the first row.

waypoints.description: Keyed by row index, as a string: "0" is the first row.

StationOutcome.description: What became of one airport that was asked.

reason.description: Why it was not reached. Null when it was.

RenderAvailability.description: What could not be had, and why. Missing data is said, never drawn as nothing.

airspace.description: `loading` means ask again: an empty `airspace` is not yet "none".

weather.description: Airports whose METAR was asked for, and how many answered.

RefreshBody.description: Optional. Narrows the refresh to these airports' reports -- what a cockpit checking its destination wants. Forecasts are a whole-route act and are asked for only when the whole route is.

FieldConditions.description: One airport on the route. Either the figures and the station they came from, or `absent` saying why there are none -- never a guessed number.

absent.description: Why there are no figures. Present only when there are none.

density_altitude.description: Absent when the report carries no temperature.

station.description: Whose report this is. `distance_nm` of 0 is the airport's own; anything else is borrowed, and from how far.

RenderColumns.description: The nav log's columns, in order, as the printed sheet carries them.

items.description: One column. `fields` name the leg fields it shows, keys of `fields` in the response. A wind block is one column over two physical ones, so `widths` has one entry per physical column.

PanelTokenResponse.description: The pairing was confirmed. This body is returned exactly once.

label.description: What this pairing is called in account settings, until renamed.

token.description: Present as `Authorization: Bearer`. It never expires and is revoked from account settings, so store it where the panel will find it again.

fields.description: Each field's unit, type and, where a wrong guess is expensive, its sign convention -- once per response rather than on every field object. `var` is positive WEST, the opposite of the WMM convention.

terrain.description: Null when no terrain could be had; `availability.terrain` says why.

RenderTimeline.description: The Flight Timeline, placed. Every `*_pct` is a position across the band, so it holds at any width; `nm` figures are along the route.

flight.description: The flight line: bends as `{nm, ft, kind}`, and its transitions.

climb.description: gallons for the climb phase — the rate beside it is climb_gph
climb.title: climb fuel

climb_gph.description: the plan's own climb rate, seeded from the aircraft profile's climb_gph and written by the pilot; every leg up to the TOC burns at it
climb_gph.title: climb burn rate

cruise.description: gallons for the cruise phase — the rate beside it is cruise_gph
cruise.title: cruise fuel

cruise_gph.description: the plan's own cruise rate, seeded from the aircraft profile's cruise_gph and written by the pilot; every leg after the TOC burns at it
cruise_gph.title: cruise burn rate

reserves_gph.description: the rate the reserve is counted at — cruise_gph unless the pilot says otherwise
reserves_gph.title: reserve burn rate

reserves_minutes.description: minutes of reserve to hold back; 45 unless the whole flight lands in daylight
reserves_minutes.title: reserve duration

Waypoint.description: A checkpoint. The fields a pilot writes carry the Field shape; the record behind them -- frequencies, the airport data -- is plain, because wrapping a list of frequencies would claim it is a cell on the sheet.

airport_info.description: Field elevation is read live, never from the saved copy.

CockpitPlan.description: The plan a paired cockpit shows, and which rule chose it.

binding.description: `explicit` -- the pilot sent this plan with "Send to sim". `last_touched` -- nothing was sent, so this is their most recently updated plan. Show which: a default that says so is not ambient.

working_sheet.description: The plan this account is in the middle of, by id alone. It is not one of `plans`: the shelf is what the pilot asked to keep.

Field.description: One field, always the same shape: what the pilot entered, and every slot behind it. `value` is null for a `suggested` field -- the number there is the calculator's own offer, not theirs.

state.description: Read this, not the value, to learn whether a write landed.

suggestion.description: A value offered from outside the engine.

PairResponse.description: A pairing in flight: what to show, and what to poll with.

code.description: Six characters for the panel to display, hyphenated. Drawn from Crockford Base32, so it carries no I, L, O or U -- the glyphs a pilot misreads through a headset.

poll_after_ms.description: How long to wait between polls. Polling faster spends the shared per-address budget on one pairing and earns a 429.

poll_token.description: Keep this. It is what the panel polls with, and it is never shown.

PairingPending.description: Nobody has typed the code yet. Keep polling.

panel.description: A paired cockpit's token, from `POST /api/v1/panel/pair`. It never expires and is revoked from account settings.

info.description: The nav-log plan as a REST resource. FOR FLIGHT SIMULATION USE ONLY — NOT FOR REAL AVIATION. Built but not promised: there is no published stability contract for this surface until a consumer asks for one.
info.title: SimNavLog

get.description: The plan the pilot sent with "Send to sim", or their most recently updated one -- and always which of the two rules chose it, so a default can say so rather than looking like a decision.

404.description: No such plan, or not this account's.

429.description: This caller is over its budget. `Retry-After` says how long to wait.
